Team —

Thanks for a productive weekly today. Two quick asks as we lock down QBR materials and surface exec asks:

1) Action census: I attached the current tracker (updated-action-tracker-20260831.csv) with owners and current status. Please update your rows by EOD Tuesday (8/31) with: status, blockers, and estimated close date.

2) Exec asks: Finance wants a short note on the SLA exception request from Acme Payments (they're pushing for a revenue credit until we can meet 99.9% dedicated latency). I’ve added a row in the SLA-exception-log.csv — we need an internal recommendation (approve/deny/conditional) + risks by Wednesday 9/1 COB.

Key items pulled from today's discussion (owners):
- Payment connector (Marissa) — prod spec + integration test plan (deliverable needed 9/14)
- Model pin + rollback policy (Karthik) — confirm model variant & canary plan (ETA 9/7)
- Canary/fallback for Acme (Vivek + Sean) — propose policy that meets exec tolerance and minimizes revenue risk (ETA 9/1)
- Pricing/credit recommendation (Jordan) — coordinate with Finance and sales (ETA 9/2)

Please don't reply-all with long threads — update the tracker and if you have a short clarifying note, add it inline and cc me. I'm attaching the current QBR deck slices and the SLA exception log for reference.

Attachments: [QBR-readout-deck-v2.pptx (pptx)], [SLA-exception-log.csv (csv)], [updated-action-tracker-20260831.csv (csv)]

Thanks —
Olga

Thanks, Olga. Quick clarifying point on the "Model pin + rollback policy" line:

- Are we asking for a single pinned variant for Acme's Dedicated pool, or a staged variant that degrades to a quantized fallback? The canary requirements differ (latency SLO vs quality guardrails).
- Our current infra lead flagged capacity for the dedicated tier in us-west2 as tight in mid-September — if the pin requires a heavy variant, we may need to push the canary start back.

I can scope a short doc by 9/1 with the trade-offs (latency/cost/quality) if that helps exec decisioning. Also, looping in Sean since he owns the deployment gating.

On the SLA exception: I'm +1 for a conditional approval if we can guarantee a fallback path (quantized variant + KV cache policy) for spikes. Will add notes to the SLA-exception-log.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Inference Platform

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional weekly sync - action census & QBR prep (exec asks)

Following up on canary/fallback design. Proposed approach (short):

1) Two-phase canary for Acme: small % (2%) using production heavy variant for 48 hours -> expand to 10% for 72 hours. If error rate or P95 latency crosses thresholds, automatic rollback to quantized variant.
2) During the canary window we enable prefix caching for payment flows and a hardened rate limiter to protect users.
3) For the exec SLA ask: recommend "conditional approval" that ties any credit to a mutually agreed remediation plan and clear metrics to accept back full SLA. I'll record the proposal in SLA-exception-log.csv and tag rows with thresholds.

Sean — can you confirm the automation hooks required for auto-rollback and whether we have the playbook to run this safely?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability
